thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks Set For 2nd Day Of Gains, But Off Highs After Trump Says Iran Decision Imminent

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks Set For 2nd Day Of Gains, But Off Highs After Trump Says Iran Decision Imminent
text:
By Barbara Kollmeyer, MarketWatch , Ryan Vlastelica and Anneken Tappe
U.S. stocks pared their gains in late-afternoon Monday with less than an hour to go until the close, following a tweet from President Donald Trump that he would make an announcement regarding the nuclear deal with Iran on Tuesday.
Earlier, stocks had gotten a lift from energy companies which rallied in response to a rise in the price of crude oil, which delivered a boost to the energy sector.
How are the main benchmarks performing?
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 39 points, or 0.2%, to 24,303. The S&P 500 index added 7 points to 2,670, a gain of 0.3%. The Nasdaq Composite Index rose 55 points, or 0.8%, to 7,263. All three indexes were off their session highs.
Both the S&P and the Nasdaq were set for their second straight positive session, while the Dow could post a third, including a slight gain of 0.02% on Thursday. Monday's advance built on a sharp rally in Friday's session, which was the largest for the Dow since April 10.
The day's gains were broad, with seven of the 11 S&P 500 sectors higher on the day. Energy was by far the biggest gainer, up 1.6%, followed by information technology, which gained 1.1%
What's driving markets?
President Trump tweeted the would make an announcement on a possible decertification of the Iran (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-says-hell-announce-his-iran-nuclear-deal-decision-on-tuesday-2018-05-07) nuclear agreement that the Obama administration had reached with the Middle Eastern country back in 2015. European leaders had urged Trump not to abandon the pact.
(https://twitter.com/realDonaldTrump/status/993562242124865536)
Trump had until Saturday to decide whether to keep the deal intact. Abandoning it would trigger a reimposition of economic sanctions on Iran, hampering oil exports from the country and cutting global supply.
Meanwhile, U.S. oil benchmark came off its high in electronic trading (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-pulls-back-in-electronic-trade-as-trump-sets-iran-deal-decision-announcement-for-tuesday-2018-05-07), pulling back from its highest level since 2014 (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-above-70-for-the-first-time-since-2014-as-investors-await-us-decision-on-iran-2018-05-07) that it had reached earlier.
Global trade headlines will also be in focus for investors, after a team of U.S. negotiators weren't able to secure a trade agreement after multiday talks with counterparts in Beijing. China state media indicated that talks were positive, and more negotiations would be needed to avoid a trade war, the South China Morning Post reported (http://www.scmp.com/news/china/policies-politics/article/2144982/state-media-strikes-positive-tone-over-china-us-trade).
Read:After earnings barrage and data, stock-market moves now hinge on global trade (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/after-earnings-barrage-and-data-stock-market-moves-now-hinge-on-global-trade-2018-05-05)
Also on the trade front, officials from Canada, Mexico and the U.S. met in Washington for another round of discussions regarding the North American Free Trade Agreement. Market participants expect the parties to reach a deal in principle this month.
Richmond Federal President Tom Barkin, meanwhile, kicked off the of the trio of Fed speakers scheduled for the afternoon, saying inflation was stable and there was no need for the Fed to step up its pace in the current economy environment.
Barkin was expected to be followed by remarks from Chicago Federal Reserve Bank President Charles Evans and Dallas Fed President Robert Kaplan, who will both speak at the 23rd Annual Financial Markets Conference in Amelia Island, Fla., at 3:30 p.m. Eastern.
In economic data, consumer credit rose 3.6% in March (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/consumer-credit-growth-in-march-slowest-in-six-months-as-credit-card-use-drops-2018-05-07).
What are strategists saying?
"We're waiting on more clarity about the Iran deal. If Trump pulls out, which other leaders have urged him not to do, then supply will be cut, which will have the same impact as rising demand in terms of driving up prices. But even beyond that, we're entering the summer driving season and the energy sector has been down for so long that it looks poised for a rebound," said Mark Martiak, senior wealth strategist at Premier Wealth/First Allied.
"Beyond that, there are no obvious catalysts on the horizon, which leaves more room for geopolitical risk to impact trading. I think valuations are fair, but I also expect we'll see a lot more volatility going forward."
Which stocks are in focus?
Energy stocks earlier rose broadly alongside the gain in oil, but pared gains following Trump's tweet. Chevron Corp.'s(CVX) stock fell 0.7%, while Exxon Mobil Corp. (XOM) shares were still up 0.9%. ConocoPhillips(COP) shares were little changed.
First-quarter earnings season remains in focus, though the vast majority of S&P 500 companies have already posted their results.
Read:The stock market is punishing companies that beat earnings forecasts--here's what history says it means (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dont-panic-when-the-stock-market-punishes-companies-for-good-earnings-2018-05-07)
Also check out:Here's why 'peak earnings' don't mean its all downhill for the stock market (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/heres-why-peak-earnings-dont-mean-its-all-downhill-for-the-stock-market-2018-05-07)
Tyson Foods Inc.(TSN) reported quarterly earnings and sales that missed analyst forecasts (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/tyson-foods-shares-slip-after-earnings-and-sales-miss-consensus-2018-05-07). Shares rose 0.1%.
Sempra Energy(SRE) unexpectedly reported a drop in its first-quarter revenue (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/sempra-energy-posts-surprise-revenue-decline-2018-05-07). Adjusted earnings also came in below forecasts. The stock fell 0.8%.
Sysco Corp.(SYY) shares climbed 2.1% after the company reported earnings that came in above expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/syscos-stock-rallies-after-profit-rises-beats-expectations-2018-05-07).
Cognizant Technology Solutions Corp.'s stock (CTSH) sank 4.8% after it provided an outlook that was below expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/cognizant-technologys-stock-sinks-after-profit-matches-expectations-but-guidance-is-below-2018-05-07).
Starbucks Corp.(SBUX) shares were down 0.4% after Nestlé SA(NESN.EB) (NESN.EB) earlier said it has reached a deal to market the coffee chain's consumer and food service products. Starbucks will receive a $7.15 billion upfront payment as part of the deal.
Athenahealth Inc.(ATHN) shares jumped more than 16% after CNBC reported that Elliott Management plans to make (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/athenahealth-shares-surge-20-on-report-of-7-bln-elliott-management-bid-2018-05-07) a $7 billion bid for the company.
Gramercy Property Trust's (GPT) stock surged 15.5% after the commercial real-estate asset management company said it would be acquired by Blackstone Group LP (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/gramercy-propertys-stock-soars-after-blackstones-76-billion-buyout-deal-2018-05-07)(BX) in a cash deal valued at $7.6 billion.
Shares of International Flavors & Fragrances Inc.(IFF) fell 10.7% after announcing a $7.1 billion stock-and-cash deal (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/international-flavors-fragrances-to-acquire-frutarom-in-71-billion-deal-2018-05-07) to acquire Israel-based Frutarom Industries, Ltd..
Shares of Berkshire Hathaway Inc.(BRKA) (BRKA) rose 0.9% after the multinational conglomerate said over the weekend it swung to a rare loss in the first quarter due to lower insurance premiums and an accounting rule change. (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/buffetts-berkshire-hathaway-books-rare-first-quarter-loss-on-investments-2018-05-05)
At the Berkshire shareholder meeting on Saturday, chairman Warren Buffett commented on a range of topics. He applauded Apple Inc.'s (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/warren-buffett-applauds-apples-share-buybacks-2018-05-05)(AAPL) share buybacks, defended a stake in Wells Fargo & Co (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/warren-buffett-defends-wells-fargo-stake-2018-05-05).(WFC) and explained why (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/warren-buffett-explains-why-he-doesnt-own-microsoft-shares-2018-05-05) he doesn't invest in Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) shares. He said bonds are a 'terrible investment' (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/buffett-bonds-are-terrible-investment-at-anything-near-current-yields-2018-05-05) near current yields and cryptocurrencies "will come to bad endings." (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/warren-buffett-says-cryptocurrencies-will-come-to-bad-endings-2018-05-05)
Plus:Buffett on why Berkshire invests in gun stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/buffett-just-offered-a-simple-explanation-why-berkshire-still-invests-in-gun-stocks-2018-05-05)
And:Buffett says health partnership will have CEO in a 'couple months' (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/buffett-says-health-partnership-will-likely-have-ceo-in-couple-months-2018-05-05)
What are other markets doing?
European stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-climb-boosted-by-nestle-after-starbucks-deal-2018-05-07) climbed higher on Monday, while Asian stocks finished mostly higher (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/china-stocks-lead-asia-higher-lifted-by-commodities-2018-05-07).
The ICE U.S. Dollar Index rose to a four-month high (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dollar-marches-to-4-month-high-as-oil-rally-points-to-higher-inflation-2018-05-07), up 0.2% at 92.760. Gold futures for June 2018 settled slightly lower (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/gold-dented-by-surging-dollar-oil-price-2018-05-07).
--Barbara Kollmeyer contributed to this article
